result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_smallworld_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a Watts-Strogatz small-world graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3965-L4022){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_smallworld_graph( n, k=6, p=0.1, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Small-world graph](/assets/graphs/add-smallworld-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three Watts-Strogatz graphs on a ring of eight nodes with k=4 and rewiring probability p=0, 0.2, and 1. At p=0 every node links to its two nearest neighbors on each side; at p=0.2 three edges are rewired into accent-colored shortcuts across the ring; at p=1 most edges are rewired and the lattice is gone." width="100%"} Creates a ring lattice with rewiring probability `p`, producing graphs with high clustering and short path lengths. Small-world networks model many real-world phenomena. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes to add. [k]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[6]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Each node connected to k nearest neighbors (must be even). [p]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Probability of rewiring each edge (`0.0` to `1.0`). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The graph starts as a ring where each node connects to its `k` nearest neighbors, then each edge is randomly rewired with probability `p`. Even a small rewiring probability is enough to shrink average path lengths dramatically while barely denting the ring's high clustering -- the hallmark of a small-world network: ::: {#292f035d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_smallworld_graph(n=100, k=6, p=0.1, seed=23) ) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 300) ``` ::: :::
